subject.title: [Bug]: Ctrl+C not working in Windows install on foreground

question: Should this issue wait for native Windows npm-global Ctrl+C reproduction before a new fix PR is queued?
rationale: The code already handles delivered SIGINT, so the remaining uncertainty is whether the failure is Windows shell/npm-shim signal delivery or gateway shutdown after delivery; choosing the fix layer without that proof risks another speculative branch.

options.title: Require Windows live repro
options.body: Keep this open until a Windows-capable maintainer or reporter validates current main or the latest package in PowerShell, cmd.exe, and Windows Terminal.

options.title: Queue after delivery proof
options.body: If live proof confirms Ctrl+C is not delivered to the foreground process, queue a narrow run-loop or launcher repair with terminal-state cleanup tests and Windows package proof.

options.title: Close if current release passes
options.body: If a native Windows npm-global run on the latest release shuts down cleanly with Ctrl+C, close as no longer reproducible with the exact release and shell evidence.

recommendation.title: Require Windows live repro
recommendation.body: Keep this open until a Windows-capable maintainer or reporter validates current main or the latest package in PowerShell, cmd.exe, and Windows Terminal.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is repeated gateway CLI lifecycle and native Windows gateway setup work near this path.
